manual: Experimental Instruction Manual: Snow or Granular Material Sliding off Steep vs Shallow RoofI. Basic Experiment Information1. Experiment Title: Comparison of Granular Material Sliding on Steep and Shallow Roofs2. Subject: Architecture & Urban Planning3. Experiment Objective: To demonstrate how roof slope affects the sliding behavior of snow or granular materials, and to understand the role of gravity and friction in roof design.II. Experimental EquipmentTwo model roofs of identical material and surface texture; support stand to hold roofs side by side; white granular material (simulating snow); spoon or shaker for sprinkling; camera for close-up observation.III. Experimental Procedure1. Preparation: Fix the two model roofs side by side on a stand, ensuring the left roof has a gentle slope and the right roof has a steeper slope. Confirm both roofs are made of the same material and are clean and dry.2. Sprinkling Operation: Using the spoon or shaker, simultaneously and evenly sprinkle the same amount of white granular material onto the upper sections of both roofs.3. Observation Operation: Keep the camera focused on both roofs as the granular material begins to move under gravity.4. Completion: Allow the granular material to finish sliding or settling, then stop the recording.IV. Observation of Experimental Phenomena1. Initial State: White granular material rests on both roofs after sprinkling.2. During Sliding: On the gentle roof, the material slides slowly or partially accumulates; on the steep roof, the material slides down quickly and more completely.3. Final State: More granular material remains on the gentle roof, while most material has slid off the steep roof.V. Summary of Experimental PrinciplesThe experiment demonstrates that roof slope affects the balance between gravitational force and friction. A steeper slope increases the component of gravity parallel to the roof surface, making it easier for snow or granular material to overcome friction and slide off. Gentler slopes have a smaller gravitational component, causing material to slide more slowly or remain in place. This principle is important in architectural roof design for snow management and structural safety.
high_level_evaluation_guide: Target concept: Roof slope influences the sliding behavior of snow or granular materials through gravity–friction balance. Minimum assumptions: two roofs of identical material, one gentle and one steep; gravity acts downward; granular material behaves as a loose solid. Expected phenomena storyline: (1) Two roofs are shown side by side with clear slope contrast; (2) white granular material is sprinkled onto both roofs at the same time; (3) material begins to move—slow or partial movement on the gentle roof, rapid sliding on the steep roof; (4) final contrast where the steep roof is mostly cleared while the gentle roof retains material. Camera should maintain a stable, frontal or slightly angled view to allow direct comparison of motion on both roofs.
